Carey Jr.''' (born February 25, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. He finished his high school career at NSU University School as a five star recruit and among the top-ranked players in the 2019 class. {{cite web|url=http://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/index.ssf/2018/01/vernon_carey_jr_recruiting_top.html|title=Vernon Carey Jr. recruiting: Top 2019 prospect to make first official visit to Michigan State in February (photos/video)|publisher=}} ==High school career== Carey starred for four years at [[NSU University School|University School of Nova Southeastern University]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]. During his freshman season, he averaged 18.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 2.0 blocks while leading the Sharks to a 15–9 overall record. As a sophomore, Carey averaged 22.0 points and 8.0 rebounds per game, while leading his team to a 20–7 record and a Florida district state championship. After his sophomore year, Carey was named to the 2017 [[Miami Herald]] and [[Sun Sentinel]] all-district teams as well as 2017 MaxPreps All-American honorable mention. As a junior, Carey averaged 26.0 points and 10.1 rebounds a game, while leading the Sharks to an overall record of 36–2, the Florida 5A state championship, and championships at the 2017 City of Palms Invitational and the 2017 John Wall Invitational.{{Cite news|url=https://theathletic.com/699672/2018/12/06/the-birth-of-vernon-carey-jr-duke-recruit/|title=The Birth of Vernon Carey Jr|last=Quinn|first=Brendan|date=December 6, 2018|work=www.theathletic.com|access-date=November 24, 2019}} Carey led his team to the finals at the High School National Tournament, losing in the championship game to [[Montverde Academy]] and its star, [[RJ Barrett]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-geico-nationals-championship-0331-story.html|title=Montverde rolls over University School for Geico Nationals title|last=|first=|date=|work=www.orlandosentinel.com|access-date=March 31, 2018}} Carey averaged 17.4 points and 5.3 rebounds per game on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) Circuit for his AAU team, Nike Team Florida.{{Cite news|url=https://www.d1circuit.com/roster_players/178203403.html|title=Vernon Carey Jr EYBL stats|last=|first=|date=|work=www.d1circuit.com|access-date=December 6, 2018}} Carey finished his senior season averaging 21.7 [[points per game|points]], 9.0 [[rebounds per game|rebounds]] and 1.1 blocks per game.{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/09/13/duke-blue-devils-vernon-carey-recruiting|title=Duke expecting big things from five-star big man Vernon Carey Jr|last=Caron|first=Emily|date=September 13, 2019|work=www.si.com|access-date=November 24, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== On December 6, 2018, Carey announced on [[Sportscenter]] that he was committed to attend [[Duke University]].
